concepts.name: Electric current
concepts.summary: Current is the rate of flow of charge, measured in amperes with an ammeter in series.
concepts.quote: Electric current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor.

concepts.name: Potential difference (voltage)
concepts.summary: The energy given to each coulomb of charge, measured in volts with a voltmeter in parallel.
concepts.quote: Charge flows round a circuit only if something pushes it.

concepts.name: Resistance
concepts.summary: Opposition to current, measured in ohms. Depends on length, thickness, material and temperature.
concepts.quote: This opposition to the flow of current is called resistance.

concepts.name: Ohm's law
concepts.summary: V = I x R links potential difference, current and resistance.
concepts.quote: Ohm’s law links the three quantities.

concepts.name: Series circuits
concepts.summary: One path: same current everywhere, potential differences add, resistances add.
concepts.quote: In a series circuit the components are connected one after another, so there is only one path for the charge to follow.
